title: Untrusted length prefix used directly as allocation size (2 sites)
description:
A length field read from an external peer is used verbatim as a `vec![0u8; n]` size, with no upper bound. CLAUDE.md security defaults: "always treat input as untrusted at system boundaries."

- persona-nmh/src/main.rs:42-43 — `let len = u32::from_le_bytes(len_buf) as usize; let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];` on the Native Messaging frame from browser stdin. The Chrome Native Messaging protocol caps extension-to-host messages at 1 MiB; a compromised or buggy extension sending `0xFFFFFFFF` makes the host attempt a 4 GiB allocation and abort. `write_message` (line 48-54) likewise does not enforce the host-to-extension cap.
- persona-attestors/src/ssh.rs:61-62 — `let resp_len = u32::from_be_bytes(len_buf) as usize; let mut resp = vec![0u8; resp_len];` on the SSH agent reply. `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is an env-supplied path; anything the user can point it at can return a 4 GiB length and OOM personad.

Both then `read_exact` into the buffer, so a bogus length also hangs until the peer disconnects.

Fix: reject lengths above a protocol-appropriate constant before allocating — 1 MiB for Native Messaging (the spec's own limit), 256 KiB is generous for an SSH agent identities answer. Return the existing error types (`anyhow` / `AttestorError::Unavailable`) rather than allocating.
close_reason: HALF STALE; the live half fixed in fe25f35. persona-attestors/src/ssh.rs was ALREADY bounded -- MAX_AGENT_REPLY is checked before vec![0u8; resp_len] (ssh.rs:93-98), and read_string bounds-checks against the remaining slice. Nothing to do there. persona-nmh was still unbounded and is now fixed. The bead's external premise was WRONG and was checked against Chrome's own documentation rather than taken on trust: it says 'the Chrome Native Messaging protocol caps extension-to-host messages at 1 MiB'. Chrome's limits are the other way round -- 64 MiB extension-to-host, 1 MB host-to-extension. So 1 MiB would have been both too small for the documented protocol and far too large to be a useful bound. Requests are capped at 64 KiB, justified by this host's own protocol (the largest request it understands is a fetch_jwt carrying a list of audiences) rather than by any external number; responses are capped at the 1 MB Chrome actually enforces, so overshooting is reported here instead of Chrome killing the host silently. read_message/write_message now take a reader and writer so the framing is testable; six tests added against frames built by python struct, all four mutations verified to kill the intended test.
